chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man whose slave married a woman without his permission and consummated the marriage with her, then his master came to know of that. He said:

That is for his master: if he wishes, he may separate them, and if he wishes, he may approve their marriage. If he does so and separates them, then the woman is entitled to whatever dower he gave her, unless he exceeded bounds and gave her a large dower. But if he approves his marriage, then they remain upon their first marriage.

So I said to Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام: then in the basis of the marriage, he had been disobedient. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: He only did something lawful, and he was not disobedient to Allah. He only disobeyed his master, and he did not disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, that is not like his doing what Allah has forbidden him of marriage during a waiting period and the like of that.

key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period during which marriage is forbidden
key_terms.فَرَّقَ: separated the spouses by dissolving the union
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master who holds authority over the slave in this matter

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave marries without his master's permission in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal status of a slave who contracts marriage without his master's permission. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that the master may either validate or dissolve the marriage, and that the act itself is not disobedience to Allah when the marriage is intrinsically halal, though it is disobedience to the master.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4548 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man whose slave married a woman without his permission and then consummated the marriage. Later, the master found out about it.
Imam (as) said:

"It is up to the master - if he wishes, he can separate them, and if he wishes, he can approve their marriage. If the master separates them, the woman is entitled to whatever dowry was given to her unless it was excessive, in which case it is reduced. But if the master approves their marriage, they remain upon their original marriage contract."

I then said to Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as): "Was the slave sinful in entering into the marriage without permission in the first place?"
Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) replied:
"What he did was something permissible and lawful; he did not disobey Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. Rather, he disobeyed his master but did not violate any law of Allah (swt).
This is not like committing something forbidden by Allah (swt), such as marrying a woman who is in her waiting period or similar acts."
